To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proteome analysis of the CM released from the spinal cord after SCI, revealed that the lesion site-dependent release of molecules, which might be related to neuroprotective and neuroregenerative processes.
the proteome of the lesioned spinal cord is highly dynamic, and the release of specific molecules is dependent upon the rostro-cautal location and time after injury.

(i) Proteomics analysis revealed that the spinal cord lesion and adjacent rostro-caudally segments released specific proteins, which are related to inflammatory and neurotrophin pathways, (ii) The conditioned media from the rostral and lesion spinal cord segments induced microglial activation and enhanced DRGs neurite growth in vitro, while the conditioned media from caudal segment induced microglial apoptosis and inhibited DRGs outgrowth, (iii) The expression of CX3CR receptor was increased
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the molecular environment in different spinal segments following SCI.
the molecular characterization of the micro-environmental changes along the rostral/caudal axis in the acute phase of SCI.
the characterization of the molecular environment within the spinal cord after SCI, which could be useful for the development of therapeutic strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rostro-caudoal gradient of the spinal cord is maintained after SCI.
the rostral segment is a source of neuroprotective molecules and the caudal segment is a source mainly of inflammatory factors.

the CM from each spinal cord segment after SCI, may have a specific effect in terms of inflammatory or trophic factors, and this could contribute to a better understanding of the regionalization of spinal cord injury.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the molecular environment in the rostro-cautal axis after spinal injury is characterized by specific protein composition, and that this may contribute to the regionalization of inflammatory and neuroprotective response in the acute injury.

we found some specific proteins at 3 days after SCI in the spinal cord central and adjacent rostral or caudal segments and we investigated some of their biological effects on microglia cells and DRGs neurites.
SCI induces a regionalized inflammatory and neurotrophins response in the injured spinal cord.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molecular environment in the rostro-cauadal axis of the injured spinal cord is different and may contribute to regionalization in terms inflammation, axonal regeneration and tissue repair.
the molecular composition of the microenvironment in the rostro-cauadl axis is not uniform after SCI.
regionalization in acute SCI is not only limited to the lesion site but may occur between the rostral and cautal segments.
